topics.title: Jessica’s Estrangement and the Zookeeper
topics.summary: Howard Stern discusses his fractured relationship with Jessica Hunt after jokes about her novel led to a rift. Gary attempts to contact her but fails, revealing anxieties surrounding the situation while Andy excitedly reports Aunt Bee's belongings being auctioned off including her bloomers.

topics.title: Sutter & Johns, Elton John, and a 'Pig'
topics.summary: The broadcast features a chaotic discussion between Sutter and Johns regarding their musical tastes – specifically Elton John’s tape and Eric Clapton. A contentious segment involves an inappropriate caller making offensive comments that are quickly censored, followed by awkward questions about sexual experiences and comparing them to age. The host struggles with editing decisions while concluding with a humorous observation about the show's format.

topics.title: Shirt Showdown and Radio Ramblings
topics.summary: A chaotic radio segment unfolds as hosts debate a t-shirt request for Stuttering John, leading to arguments about Mark Chernoff's behavior and the show’s direction. Personal opinions on Dick Clark and Ed McMahon are thrown in alongside bizarre questions regarding wardrobe choices and potential television appearances.

topics.title: Howard Stern’s Stuttering Emerson Awards Interview
topics.summary: During an interview for the Emerson Radio Awards, Howard Stern struggles with stuttering while discussing his nomination and interviewing program director Mark Chernoff. He engages in bizarre questions involving fictional characters like Ford Fairlane (a Dyson movie) and Dick Clark, punctuated by interruptions from Eddie Cantor’s grandson who laughs at him.”” 54 words.

topics.title: Ferraro and Ford Legal Troubles
topics.summary: Howard discusses Gerald Ford’s legal issues stemming from accusations of improperly influencing an election and borrowing money from a woman’s will. He recounts the fines imposed as a result, alongside Wayne Segal's persistent requests for commercial assistance and pressure to use specific phrases.

topics.title: Sales Department Frustration & Old Songs
topics.summary: During a phone call, frustration escalates over repeated attempts to contact the sales department for car issues. The conversation shifts to an old song, ‘Heart of Will You Straight,’ and discussions about past mishaps involving Wayne, Michael Segal, and a Chrysler representative, including misinterpretations regarding name changes and personal criticisms.
